title: Ashley Heights — 100 considered improvements
baseline: Proposed with brick exterior; existing owner-approved interiors retained
status: 100 local proposals, including 20 larger design alternatives prioritised for owner review; none applied to the approved house.
approvalMeaning: Approval records your preferred direction. It does not run model changes, commit code or publish. Any material design consequences will be brought back for review.

items.title: Give shallow coat storage a usable internal system
items.observation: The revised cabinet already wraps the corner and is only 320 mm deep, with coats hanging end-on.
items.proposal: Develop pull-forward coat rails, a separate wet-coat bay and removable drip trays inside the existing outline.
items.benefit: Coats become easy to retrieve without making the entrance cabinet deeper.
items.tradeoff: Rails need room to extend while someone stands in front; wet clothes need ventilation.
items.validation: Show a full winter coat, an extended rail and two people arriving without blocking the door.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Make the shoe bench work for boots and bags
items.observation: The existing bench sits under gym glazing and has a clear seated approach.
items.proposal: Divide its storage into everyday shoes, one taller boot bay and a temporary bag landing; keep the top largely clear.
items.benefit: Supports actual arrival routines without another piece of hall furniture.
items.tradeoff: A boot bay reduces the total number of shoe slots.
items.validation: Check typical shoe/boot sizes and the occupied bench against the adjoining route.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Replan arrival as a proper entrance sequence
items.observation: The entrance combines a double-height gallery, shallow coat storage, gym glazing and a route to the original hall.
items.proposal: Develop a coordinated arrival layout: preserve the shallow corner coat unit, place seated shoe-changing outside the through-route, and create one clear view from the front door into the original hall. Test a discreet internal glazed screen only where it improves zoning without narrowing the route.
items.benefit: The entrance becomes a usable, composed room rather than a collection of furniture along a passage.
items.tradeoff: A screen may interrupt the double-height openness; omit it if the route and sightline work better without it.
items.validation: Render arrival with doors open, coats in use and two people passing; compare the route to the current model.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Give the double-height entrance separate lighting scenes
items.observation: The gallery is double-height and connects directly to the original hall.
items.proposal: Develop arrival, evening and cleaning scenes using concealed ambient light, restrained wall light and useful task light at storage.
items.benefit: Makes a tall space welcoming at night while keeping the oak/ivory architecture calm.
items.tradeoff: More circuits and control coordination; no extra pendant should compete with the existing composition.
items.validation: Compare fixed-camera evening views and confirm accessible switches at both ends.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Keep rainwater and grit at the entrance threshold
items.observation: The entrance is the main transition from a four-car forecourt into the house.
items.proposal: Detail a flush replaceable mat well and a sheltered set-down position within the existing arrival footprint.
items.benefit: Reduces tracked dirt and makes wet-weather arrival more comfortable.
items.tradeoff: Threshold depth, drainage and door clearances must be coordinated before specifying a mat.
items.validation: Draw threshold section, open door and mat replacement access.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Compose one clear view from the front door
items.observation: The entrance links several angled spaces; earlier brochure views obscured this relationship.
items.proposal: Choose one restrained artwork or lit plaster surface as the arrival focus and align the normal eye-level camera with the real route.
items.benefit: Gives arrival a legible destination without adding more furniture.
items.tradeoff: The focus must not hide glazing, structure or the coat cupboard.
items.validation: Review the actual door-open view and reverse view in the native model, without wide-angle distortion.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Test the kitchen with two cooks and the dishwasher open
items.observation: The accepted Quiet oak kitchen has a compact 1.05 x 1.60 m island and several adjoining social routes.
items.proposal: Create an occupied-use plan and refine only handles, door hinging or local fittings if the fridge/dishwasher/cooking routines conflict.
items.benefit: Protects the chosen appearance while making everyday use more convincing.
items.tradeoff: Any required cabinet adjustment must preserve the selected island and accepted room arrangement where possible.
items.validation: Run cooking, unloading and garden-passage scenarios with actual appliance door envelopes.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Turn the kitchen tall run into a pantry and appliance wall
items.observation: The kitchen has a compact island and multiple social routes; more freestanding appliances or island enlargement would compete with circulation.
items.proposal: Reconfigure the existing tall cabinetry into an integrated pantry, breakfast station and appliance bank. Keep the chosen island and main plumbing positions; use the tall run to take everyday clutter and preparation away from its social edge.
items.benefit: A more capable kitchen with a coherent storage wall and a clearer island for cooking and conversation.
items.tradeoff: Pantry capacity competes with appliance and general storage; final cabinet allocation depends on actual equipment.
items.validation: Model doors and pull-outs open, check appliance ventilation and two-person use, and compare retained cabinet capacity.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Make waste sorting part of the preparation route
items.observation: The kitchen study establishes preparation, cooking and dining but the selected brief does not record a household waste capacity target.
items.proposal: Allocate labelled removable recycling, food-waste and general-waste bins within the existing base units near preparation.
items.benefit: Reduces trips and avoids loose bins beside the island.
items.tradeoff: Bin capacity competes with pan storage.
items.validation: Show a chopping-to-bin routine and full-bin removal without blocking appliance doors.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Refine island socket and cable placement
items.observation: The island is an accepted social and preparation centre, not just a visual feature.
items.proposal: Locate discreet accessible power on an end face away from seated knees and wet preparation, with cable routes contained inside joinery.
items.benefit: Makes occasional appliances and laptops usable without trailing leads across a route.
items.tradeoff: Socket location must be coordinated with drawers, overhang and electrical design.
items.validation: Demonstrate a mixer and laptop in use with all cables clear of standing and seated circulation.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Light the working edge without glare
items.observation: The kitchen palette relies on pale stone and oak, which should remain the visual focus.
items.proposal: Refine concealed task lighting to illuminate worktops from in front of users, with separate dining dimming and no exposed LED dots.
items.benefit: Improves preparation visibility while retaining a soft evening atmosphere.
items.tradeoff: Diffusers and drivers need accessible replacement space.
items.validation: Review cooking-eye and seated-eye views at day and night, including reflections in stone and glazing.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Create an integrated garden-dining bay
items.observation: The garden dining space is generous in appearance but its occupied chair and garden-door routes need to work together.
items.proposal: Compare a tailored banquette along a suitable solid wall with the current freestanding dining arrangement, integrating serving storage at one end and retaining a large everyday table. Keep garden glazing and door openings clear.
items.benefit: A more architectural dining area with a defined place in the open-plan room and potentially clearer circulation.
items.tradeoff: A banquette is less flexible and inner seats are harder to reach; do not proceed if no suitable uninterrupted wall exists.
items.validation: Test the current table size with people seated, chair pullback, serving and open garden doors before choosing the bay.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Give garden dining controllable afternoon light
items.observation: Garden dining is deliberately placed in the bright rear extension.
items.proposal: Study discreet external shading or recessed blinds that preserve the glazing and roof form, then choose the least intrusive option.
items.benefit: Reduces glare and makes the room comfortable across more of the day.
items.tradeoff: External shading can affect the elevation; solar performance needs assessment rather than a visual guess.
items.validation: Compare seasonal sun positions, table-eye glare and the closed-blind appearance before committing.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Centre an eight-seat round table in the hexagonal dining bay
items.observation: The current rectangular extending table sits east of the centre of the formal dining bay. The owner requested a round table with eight regular places centred in that area.
items.proposal: Compare a 1.70 m round oak pedestal table at the dining bay centre, with eight of the current upholstered chairs equally spaced around it. Re-centre the pendant and keep the lounge, windows, hall doors and drinks cabinet.
items.benefit: A clearer focal point that follows the room shape and gives all eight diners equal access to conversation.
items.tradeoff: Eight permanent chairs occupy more of the room every day. The west/northwest chairs are close to the drinks cabinet; access behind occupied chairs and cabinet opening must be reviewed. This option replaces the previous six-seat extending brief for comparison only.
items.validation: Inspect matched native model photos and a dimensioned chair/pullback plan. Confirm door swings, cabinet access and circulation with chairs occupied and pulled out.
items.planCaption: Proposed round-table plan from the preview coordinates. Eight dining chair positions and 400 mm pullback outlines; 1 m scale bar. Concept, not measured survey.

items.title: Store the extension leaf and spare chairs deliberately
items.observation: The formal table is extendable; the source specification does not assign a storage location for its leaf or extra chairs.
items.proposal: Reserve accessible protected leaf storage and a home for occasional chairs in existing nearby joinery or the garage store.
items.benefit: Avoids a beautiful table that is inconvenient to extend.
items.tradeoff: Leaf storage can consume a long cupboard; stacking chairs must still fit the room style.
items.validation: Record real folded/stacked sizes and demonstrate one-person retrieval.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Refine the drinks cabinet as a serving station
items.observation: A 430 mm-deep drinks cabinet already exists at the dining end.
items.proposal: Fit a removable spill tray, glass dividers and a discreet preparation light inside the existing cabinet, retaining the warm neutral finish.
items.benefit: Turns the approved drinks area into a practical hosting detail.
items.tradeoff: Useful worktop space must take priority over display bottles and ornaments.
items.validation: Show a host preparing two drinks while guests pass and the cooler door opens.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Give each formal sofa a proper reading position
items.observation: Two facing sofas make a conversation group; the central table alone is not equally reachable from every seat.
items.proposal: Add or reposition compact end tables and shaded reading lights at the outer sofa ends, with concealed power.
items.benefit: Supports books and drinks without changing the accepted sofa style or colour.
items.tradeoff: Too many objects would clutter the room; use only where reach is poor.
items.validation: Check seated reach, shade glare and door routes from all four sofa ends.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Complete the office desk power feed
items.observation: The office already has an underside cable tray, grommet and monitor lead. The modelled cable stops at the desk; a room-to-desk supply route is not established by those details.
items.proposal: Resolve the final wall/floor-to-desk power and data route, retaining the existing tray and grommet and keeping the chair path clear.
items.benefit: Keeps the open desk arrangement tidy and safe to use.
items.tradeoff: Floor feeds can require construction work; a perimeter solution may be less invisible.
items.validation: Trace power/data to the wall and show the chair rotating and pulling back.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

references.title: HSE: workstation space, glare and screen position

items.title: Control video-call light at the bay
items.observation: The retained bay is the office daylight source and the desk is deliberately side-lit.
items.proposal: Coordinate a translucent daytime blind with a monitor/camera position that keeps the face evenly lit and avoids screen reflections.
items.benefit: Makes the office work for calls without blacking out the room.
items.tradeoff: A blind changes the filtered view; keep the existing window composition.
items.validation: Compare seated webcam framing and monitor glare in morning and afternoon conditions.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

references.title: HSE: workstation space, glare and screen position

items.title: Make the TV lounge acoustically separable
items.observation: The open relationship between kitchen and TV lounge makes cooking and television compete for the same sound space.
items.proposal: Compare a wide, pocketing glazed acoustic screen at the lounge transition, with coordinated ceiling absorption and concealed tracks. Keep it fully open for everyday family use and closed for films or calls.
items.benefit: A separate quiet room when useful while retaining the visual connection and accepted palette.
items.tradeoff: Pocket walls, track depth and acoustic seals need space; ordinary decorative sliding glass will not provide the same isolation.
items.validation: Model the screen open and closed, check the parked leaves, thresholds and fixed TV sightlines; assess the actual assembly acoustically.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Give both bed occupants complete night controls
items.observation: The accepted bed is against the south wall with two 600 mm bedsides and a fixed TV.
items.proposal: Coordinate reading light, low night light, main-light off and charging at both bedsides without changing the headboard.
items.benefit: Makes the room feel luxurious through daily convenience rather than a new visual theme.
items.tradeoff: Control plates can look busy; keep a simple repeatable layout.
items.validation: Show controls reachable from both pillows with a phone, book and water on each bedside.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Create a quiet route from bed to bathroom
items.observation: The bathroom is reached through the shifted dressing room from the main bedroom.
items.proposal: Add shielded low-level lighting on that route, with a gentle night scene and manual override.
items.benefit: Supports one person getting up without flooding the bed with light.
items.tradeoff: Sensors must not trigger unnecessarily from movement in bed.
items.validation: Review the route from both sleeping positions at night and verify no direct glare.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Make the two equal TVs behave independently
items.observation: Both principal screens are now the same size, with separate bed and sofa viewing positions.
items.proposal: Specify independent control and audio zones, including headphones for one viewer, while retaining both fixed screens.
items.benefit: Avoids operating the wrong screen and reduces conflict between study, sleep and TV.
items.tradeoff: Two open-room TVs cannot provide acoustic separation; simultaneous loud viewing remains unsuitable.
items.validation: Demonstrate one screen on, one off and individual audio control from bed, sofa and desk.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Refine the rounded L desk for working comfort
items.observation: The approved desk has equal 1.80 m arms, 700 mm depth and rounded inner/outer corners.
items.proposal: Resolve knee space, cable access and a monitor position along one arm while preserving the swivel view to the sofa TV.
items.benefit: Keeps the sculptural desk useful for actual work.
items.tradeoff: Storage below either arm can restrict chair rotation; avoid filling the corner with drawers.
items.validation: Check a seated user at both arms, chair rotation and the TV sightline with a monitor present.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

references.title: HSE: workstation space, glare and screen position

items.title: Make the garage-gable alcove an intentional window retreat
items.observation: The accepted low central opening creates a distinct space beyond the principal bedroom, not a normal standing doorway.
items.proposal: Design a complete low seated retreat beyond the opening: fitted upholstered window seating, low integrated storage and concealed reading light shaped to the unchanged roof. Keep everyday wardrobe and bathroom circulation outside it.
items.benefit: Makes the constrained volume feel deliberate and luxurious rather than leftover space.
items.tradeoff: It remains an optional duck-through destination; the low opening is not made full-height or represented as accessible.
items.validation: Render the approach and seated view using the real roof and opening; verify sitting headroom and window operation.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Refine bedroom blackout at the retained windows
items.observation: The suite has several east windows and a vaulted west alcove; the accepted layout depends on their outlook.
items.proposal: Detail discreet blackout layers and side returns without changing window positions or headboard form.
items.benefit: Improves sleep and TV viewing while preserving daytime light.
items.tradeoff: Blind housings must fit the actual recesses and avoid the moved partition junctions.
items.validation: Show blinds fully raised/lowered at all openings and check service access.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Give the upstairs family lounge a shared device home
items.observation: The family lounge already has a compact homework desk, games storage and a reading sofa; chargers and tablets need a shared storage routine.
items.proposal: Reserve one ventilated charging drawer in the existing east storage run, with removable device dividers and a clear tray for current homework.
items.benefit: Keeps the small desk and games table available without adding furniture or changing the neutral palette.
items.tradeoff: Devices create heat and consume storage; the drawer needs appropriate charging hardware and ventilation.
items.validation: Show the actual family devices stored, cables managed and the drawer open without blocking the terrace or bedroom approach.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Replan the ensuite as a coherent spa room
items.observation: The larger ensuite and sculptural bath are accepted, but the fixtures need a coherent spatial composition as well as more lavish materials.
items.proposal: Compare a unified bathing and shower zone, a calmer double-vanity wall and a discreet WC sightline screen within the enlarged bathroom. Retain the bath window and wardrobe relationship; use a flush floor wherever feasible.
items.benefit: The bathroom reads as a complete luxurious room with a dry dressing edge and a deliberate bath focal point.
items.tradeoff: Moving drainage, screens or the shower can add construction work; a raised bath plinth is not assumed.
items.validation: Produce alternative occupied plans, wet/dry routes and matched 3D views; then check waste falls, cleaning access and floor support.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Protect privacy at the bath window without losing sky
items.observation: The new bath window is 1.80 m wide with a sill about 1.10 m above the bathroom floor.
items.proposal: Compare a lower privacy treatment with a discreet adjustable blind, using actual neighbour sightlines before choosing.
items.benefit: Keeps daylight and the bath focal point without unintended overlooking.
items.tradeoff: Permanent obscuration reduces the outlook; a blind needs user operation.
items.validation: Draw sightlines from relevant exterior positions to a seated bath user and standing shower user.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

references.title: Sevenoaks: Residential Extensions SPD (design and amenity guidance)

items.title: Put a dry towel within reach of the shower exit
items.observation: A towel warmer already sits on the east side of the principal bathroom. The shower is on the opposite side, so the practical reach deserves a separate check.
items.proposal: Add a compact towel hook or shelf at the shower exit if the measured reach to the existing warmer is awkward; keep the bath-side warmer and all fixture positions.
items.benefit: Adds practical spa comfort without more decorative clutter.
items.tradeoff: The new detail must not intrude into the shower approach or be soaked during use.
items.validation: Show a user stepping out of the shower and reaching a dry towel without crossing the central wet floor.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Reconcile the detailed design with a measured survey
items.observation: The planning action register explicitly says the reconstruction, boundaries, levels and floorspace are provisional; detailed furnishings now depend on them.
items.proposal: Create one survey-reconciliation issue identifying differences between measured building/topographic data and the model, with proposed local corrections ranked by impact on the accepted design.
items.benefit: Concentrates changes where real dimensions require them and protects the minimal-alteration brief.
items.tradeoff: A survey may reveal unavoidable changes; approval here is for the reconciliation approach, not spending or appointing consultants.
items.validation: Produce a dimension-difference schedule and marked plans before altering accepted rooms.

references.title: Sevenoaks: Residential Extensions SPD (design and amenity guidance)

items.title: Design the wardrobe as complete fitted dressing architecture
items.observation: The walk-through room has an important bathroom route; adding isolated furniture will make it feel busier without improving storage much.
items.proposal: Redesign the internal joinery as coordinated full-height runs with dedicated long hanging, double hanging, folded storage and a concealed dressing perch. Keep the accepted room size, mirror and through-route, with no central island.
items.benefit: More useful clothing capacity and a calmer tailored dressing room within the existing footprint.
items.tradeoff: Storage allocation must fit actual clothing; full-height joinery can feel heavy unless openings, lighting and proportions are resolved.
items.validation: Compare measured hanging lengths and drawer capacities with the baseline, showing all fronts open and the route occupied.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Add a compact sit-down dressing perch
items.observation: The wardrobe already includes a full-length mirror. The current specification does not allocate a seat for putting on shoes.
items.proposal: Test a pull-out or fold-away upholstered perch integrated into existing joinery, preserving the central bathroom route and current mirror.
items.benefit: Completes the dressing routine without enlarging the wardrobe or adding a loose chair.
items.tradeoff: The perch consumes storage and must be stable when loaded; it cannot occupy the through-route while left open.
items.validation: Show a seated user, drawers open and another person passing to the bathroom; reject the perch if those uses cannot coexist.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Separate laundry from clean dressing storage
items.observation: The bathroom and wardrobe form one daily route and already contain substantial fitted storage.
items.proposal: Reserve ventilated removable laundry bins near the bathroom end, divided only as the household actually sorts washing.
items.benefit: Stops laundry accumulating beside the bed or within clean-clothes shelves.
items.tradeoff: Bins reduce drawer capacity and need a carrying route to the utility.
items.validation: Check bin removal, carrying clearance and that the bathroom door can still open fully.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Replan the side bedroom and family-room boundary together
items.observation: The side bedroom still has a 665 mm foot turn despite usable side aisles. A shorter frame alone can recover at most a small amount.
items.proposal: Study a further local transfer of space from the family approach into the bedroom, together with a revised ensuite entrance and storage position. Compare an approximately 450 mm northward partition study with the current layout, rather than just shrinking furniture.
items.benefit: Potentially creates a genuinely comfortable double bedroom with a clearer arrival and ensuite route.
items.tradeoff: The family room loses area and its approach changes. The 450 mm shift is a test dimension, not a verified recommendation; keep its main seating and external openings usable.
items.validation: Model both rooms together, measure occupied bed/wardrobe/door routes and reject any option that trades one pinch for another.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Make the loft shower work at finished head height
items.observation: The loft suite records approximately 2.09 m dormer headroom above structural floor, before floor and ceiling finishes reduce it.
items.proposal: Draw a finished section through the shower and choose a compact head/arm arrangement and tray build-up that preserves useful head clearance, retaining the dormer roof.
items.benefit: Makes the loft ensuite credible for standing use rather than judging it from a floor plan alone.
items.tradeoff: Tall users may still find the room constrained; a low-profile fitting cannot solve an unsuitable roof height.
items.validation: Show finished floor, tray, shower head and a range of user heights in section using actual products.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Protect Bedroom 3 balcony access during dressing
items.observation: Bedroom 3 retains balcony access and its documented foot/wardrobe routes are single-file.
items.proposal: Coordinate wardrobe hardware and the window treatment so an open cupboard or blind does not trap the balcony approach.
items.benefit: Makes the compact room easier to use without moving walls.
items.tradeoff: Sliding fronts may change usable opening width; retain storage access.
items.validation: Check dressing, bed-making and balcony-door-open states separately and together where realistic.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Give the compact fourth bedroom a complete guest-room layout
items.observation: The fourth bedroom must accommodate a real bed, clothing and luggage without permanent clutter in the route.
items.proposal: Develop one coordinated bed-and-storage arrangement with full-height joinery on a suitable solid wall, an integrated occasional work/dressing surface and luggage space. Keep the accepted mattress and headboard; compare complete furniture layouts rather than extra shelves.
items.benefit: A small bedroom can work as a finished room instead of a bed surrounded by leftover pieces.
items.tradeoff: The room may not support every function simultaneously; the work surface may need to close away.
items.validation: Show sleeping, dressing and luggage-open states with all doors and windows operating in the actual shell.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Give guest luggage a proper temporary home
items.observation: The garden guest suite has substantial sliding storage, a reading chair and a fixed 43-inch TV.
items.proposal: Reserve a lower wardrobe bay or folding luggage perch sized for an open suitcase rather than adding a permanent bench in the route.
items.benefit: Guests can unpack without using the bed or blocking balcony access.
items.tradeoff: Luggage space reduces clothing storage; a folding perch needs a stored position.
items.validation: Show an open suitcase, occupied bed and ensuite door all in their normal use states.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Vary bedroom textiles while preserving approved headboards
items.observation: The owner rejected a blue headboard redesign but wants subtle variety within the same house style.
items.proposal: Prepare a restrained room-by-room textile schedule using ivory, oatmeal, warm grey and muted natural accents only on replaceable layers.
items.benefit: Gives bedrooms individual character without changing their furniture identity.
items.tradeoff: Too many finishes would fragment the house; cap each room at one quiet accent.
items.validation: Present side-by-side existing and proposed textile swatches with headboards and joinery locked.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Resolve the guest shower handle and opening together
items.observation: The guest shower concept limits its inward leaf to 85 degrees to keep a double-sided handle clear of the lining.
items.proposal: Select a compatible hinge/handle set or alternative door system that provides reliable entry inside the existing shower footprint.
items.benefit: Avoids relying on an arbitrary model stop that the real product cannot reproduce.
items.tradeoff: Changing the enclosure system can alter access and cleaning; do not shrink the shower casually.
items.validation: Use manufacturer drawings to test full travel, handle clearance, entry and emergency access.

items.title: Give shared bathrooms concealed daily-item storage
items.observation: The family bathroom and cloakroom have floating vanities, but compact counters can quickly collect toiletries.
items.proposal: Develop shallow mirror storage where construction permits and drawer dividers within existing vanities, retaining the warm neutral design.
items.benefit: Keeps the counters calm while making everyday items reachable.
items.tradeoff: A recessed cabinet needs a suitable wall; a surface unit must not project awkwardly.
items.validation: Check wall build-up, tap/mirror relationship and open cabinet access with a user at the basin.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Make the minimum-change planning case measurable
items.observation: The brief favours minimal alterations and the planning register flags front-wing scale and unverified baseline areas.
items.proposal: Prepare a retained/removed/new fabric and volume comparison for Existing, Proposed and Planning, then identify which small envelope reductions would most reduce bulk if the planning review requires them.
items.benefit: Supports an informed planning conversation while protecting the rooms and features that matter most.
items.tradeoff: No arbitrary percentage proves acceptability; this is an evidence study, not permission or approval to shrink rooms.
items.validation: Tie quantities to a verified original-house baseline, draw the street massing and list the actual room consequences of each fallback.

references.title: Sevenoaks: Residential Extensions SPD (design and amenity guidance)

items.title: Make the low loft bridge constraint visible in the design
items.observation: The retained bridge is recorded at roughly 1.78–1.90 m headroom, below comfortable standing height for some users.
items.proposal: Produce a finished-floor section and develop a clearly legible low-headroom transition; assess a local non-roof structural refinement only if feasible.
items.benefit: Prevents a seemingly normal corridor concealing a known comfort constraint.
items.tradeoff: Signs or lighting do not fix headroom; any physical improvement needs structure and stair review.
items.validation: Review a full-height human section along the complete route and label unresolved dimensions explicitly.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Check neighbour daylight before choosing further exterior refinements
items.observation: Neighbour heights and flank-window relationships are still indicative in the planning evidence, while the wing and dormers materially shape the adjoining outlook.
items.proposal: Build a verified neighbour-window and level model, then assess daylight, sunlight and outlook around the changed elevations before selecting any mitigation.
items.benefit: Directs any small roof/window/setback adjustment toward an actual concern rather than guesswork.
items.tradeoff: A specialist study may be needed; a simple diagram or 45-degree screen is not a guarantee of consent.
items.validation: Identify affected windows and outdoor spaces, state survey uncertainty and compare any mitigation against the unchanged scheme.
items.scope: Both designs and relevant neighbouring context

references.title: Sevenoaks: Residential Extensions SPD (design and amenity guidance)

items.title: Keep linen storage useful without filling the landing
items.observation: The landing already has sliding-front linen storage designed to avoid door swings into the route.
items.proposal: Assign shelf spacing to bedding sets and add removable labelled baskets for spare pillows and towels.
items.benefit: Uses existing joinery better and reduces bedroom clutter.
items.tradeoff: Oversized baskets can be awkward to carry on stairs.
items.validation: Check shelf reach and one-person removal of a full bedding set without blocking bedroom doors.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Make the loft a two-zone hobby and family room
items.observation: The large loft has several potential uses and low roof areas; a generic furniture spread does not establish how those uses coexist.
items.proposal: Develop a permanent project/work zone with concealed ongoing-project storage and a separate soft family lounge, linked by a clear high-headroom route. Test sliding internal screens only where they park entirely out of the circulation.
items.benefit: The loft becomes a destination with two convincing uses and a practical way to leave projects unfinished.
items.tradeoff: Screens and storage can make the loft feel smaller; low eaves are not counted as normal standing space and removed eaves units are not reinstated.
items.validation: Render working and cleared states; map finished headroom, stair arrival and window access before approving the layout.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Use task lighting where the loft ceiling is low
items.observation: The dormer structural headroom is about 2.09 m before finishes, so suspended fittings can be intrusive.
items.proposal: Refine shallow ceiling lighting and local table/reading lights with protected cable routes.
items.benefit: Improves usable light while preserving scarce headroom.
items.tradeoff: Surface fittings still consume depth and may glare under low ceilings.
items.validation: Draw a section through lights, standing users and the project table; review normal seated views.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Make the loft-bedroom narrow bedside purposeful
items.observation: The doorway-side bedside is only 205 mm wide to preserve the ensuite approach; the opposite side is 410 mm.
items.proposal: Design a compact wall-integrated phone/glasses pocket and reading control within that 205 mm zone, leaving the larger bedside unchanged.
items.benefit: Provides essentials on both sides without reintroducing removed eaves cabinets.
items.tradeoff: It will not function like a full bedside table; keep expectations honest.
items.validation: Check reach from the pillow and the bedroom/ensuite door paths with bedding in place.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Replan the gym and utility as a coordinated pair
items.observation: Running, rowing and strength currently rely on shared activity space. Rearranging small accessories will not create simultaneous-use capacity.
items.proposal: Compare the current rooms with a compact stacked-laundry service wall that may release part of the gym/utility boundary for a better equipment zone. Retain both gate-facing treadmills and their rear safety areas; test any partition move only after fitting the full laundry brief.
items.benefit: Could improve actual exercise use and remove the need for repeated equipment setup without enlarging the external envelope.
items.tradeoff: The utility loses area and equipment/service costs may increase. Do not claim all activities can run together unless the occupied layout proves it.
items.validation: Use selected equipment dimensions, door swings, laundry loading and service clearances in a combined two-room model.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Keep treadmill cables out of the circulation strip
items.observation: Both treadmills face the front gates and the gym doorway has already moved south.
items.proposal: Coordinate power points and protected cable routes at the front ends, avoiding the rear safety zones and doorway.
items.benefit: Retains the approved orientation while improving practical installation.
items.tradeoff: Electrical provision depends on selected machines and floor/wall construction.
items.validation: Show the actual plug/lead path for each machine and confirm no extension lead crosses a route.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Design vibration control below gym equipment
items.observation: The gym sits in the front wing below principal accommodation and includes two treadmills and free weights.
items.proposal: Develop an equipment-specific resilient floor build-up and isolated weight-drop area within the existing room.
items.benefit: Reduces disturbance and improves the feel of the gym without changing decor.
items.tradeoff: Additional floor thickness affects thresholds; acoustic benefit needs specialist assessment.
items.validation: Review equipment loads, threshold section and impact/vibration strategy before final flooring selection.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Give exercise sessions fresh air without cold draughts
items.observation: The gym room brief leaves ventilation unresolved despite multiple exercise machines.
items.proposal: Coordinate quiet supply/extract or purge ventilation with actual occupancy, avoiding air aimed directly at runners' faces.
items.benefit: Makes the room more comfortable during hard exercise.
items.tradeoff: Duct routes, plant noise and external grilles affect other design decisions.
items.validation: Assess occupancy and heat gains, then show grille locations and maintenance access in the model.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Increase cinema passing comfort with a slimmer centre table
items.observation: The current coffee table is 660 mm deep and leaves a 650 mm empty gap to the sofa. A 360 mm-deep candidate, with its screen-side edge held fixed, increases that gap to 950 mm.
items.proposal: Trial the shallower 360 mm table or remove the central table in favour of reachable console/side surfaces, keeping all four seats and the fixed screen.
items.benefit: Improves entry during a film without returning to a raised second row.
items.tradeoff: Moving the table edge away improves passage but worsens seated reach. The empty gap is not the same as clear space around occupied knees.
items.validation: Compare both layouts with realistic occupied legs, late entry and drinks reachable from each seat.
items.planCaption: Read-only concept comparison for this proposal. Nothing in the house model has been changed.

items.title: Make acoustic treatment part of the accepted dark design
items.observation: The dark fabric lining is modelled but does not establish sound isolation or acoustic performance.
items.proposal: Develop an acoustic lining and door-seal concept concealed within the current cinema palette.
items.benefit: Improves dialogue clarity and limits disturbance without changing the approved mood.
items.tradeoff: Real treatment consumes room width/depth; rerun seating and aisle checks afterward.
items.validation: Prepare wall/ceiling sections and an acoustic design review, distinguishing absorption from isolation.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Coordinate projector, speakers and service access
items.observation: The screen and seating sightlines are established, but final projector/speaker specifications remain unresolved.
items.proposal: Select a coherent equipment layout with lens throw, speaker positions, ventilation and removable access panels.
items.benefit: Avoids detailed visual equipment that cannot be installed or maintained.
items.tradeoff: Actual products may need small mounting changes; preserve screen/seat relationship where possible.
items.validation: Check manufacturer envelopes, image geometry and access for replacing each device.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Add a film-entry lighting scene
items.observation: The cinema is entered along the side of a single seating row.
items.proposal: Develop low shielded aisle guidance with a brief entrance scene and independent full cleaning light.
items.benefit: Makes late entry easier without washing out the screen.
items.tradeoff: Light spill and automatic triggering need tuning.
items.validation: Review the doorway open during a dark scene from all four seats.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Swap the games and lounge zones to open the basement route
items.observation: The earlier pool-table search held the west sofa/TV group fixed, so the only full-cue improvement was a marginal table movement.
items.proposal: Move the six-foot pool table into the west bay and move the sofa to the north wall of the east bay. Remove the separate west TV/console group and use the adjacent cinema for screen viewing; keep the bar and darts area. Test the whole zone swap with full cue envelopes.
items.benefit: A substantial reorganisation of the leisure room, with a more direct stair-to-bar route and distinct games and conversation areas.
items.tradeoff: It gives up the separate games-room TV nook. Cueing, occupied seating and access must all be checked; furniture fit alone is insufficient.
items.validation: Render the entire north room before/after, overlay the 1.525 m cue reservation and verify the circulation route around the stair and lounge.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Improve the bar through texture, not a green colour scheme
items.observation: The owner rejected the green bar treatment and wants the bar to relate more closely to the pool area.
items.proposal: Refine the bar with warm oak relief, pale stone and restrained bronze details, using the accepted pool palette as the reference.
items.benefit: Adds depth and character while keeping the house visually coherent.
items.tradeoff: Too much fluting or metallic surface can look busy; retain a calm stone counter.
items.validation: Present a material-only comparison with layout and neutral upholstery locked.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Add discreet dart storage and scorekeeping
items.observation: The model already has a protective surround, board lighting and throw line. A practical scoring and secure dart-storage position is not established in the room brief.
items.proposal: Add a flush scorekeeping panel and small closed dart/accessory drawer outside the throwing line, retaining the existing board surround and lighting.
items.benefit: Makes the activity complete without a themed pub aesthetic.
items.tradeoff: A thicker surround must not reduce the throwing distance or conflict with passage.
items.validation: Show a player scoring and storing darts without crossing another game or obstructing the normal cinema route.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Separate coolers and glasses from decorative display
items.observation: The fitted bar has a 1.302 m serving aisle, coolers, shelves and three stools.
items.proposal: Develop cooler ventilation and removable glass storage with a clear tray landing, reducing display objects where necessary.
items.benefit: Makes the bar easier to serve from and maintain while retaining its improved appearance.
items.tradeoff: Less display may look quieter; ventilation grilles need careful integration.
items.validation: Show two drinks being prepared, a cooler open and another person passing behind the host.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Rebuild the utility around stacked laundry and a drying cupboard
items.observation: The current 3.2 m service run places washer and dryer side by side with hampers, sink and tall storage.
items.proposal: Compare a stacked laundry tower with a ventilated full-height drying cupboard and a continuous sorting/folding surface in the space released. Keep the existing sink service wall, east window and both door openings where possible.
items.benefit: A utility with dedicated washing, drying and clean-folding functions rather than a row of appliances.
items.tradeoff: Stacking reduces access to the upper machine for some users; stacking hardware, ventilation and maintenance access must match real products.
items.validation: Model appliance doors, basket handling and drying contents; compare storage and clear aisle widths with the current run.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Reserve a dirty-arrival drop zone from the garage
items.observation: The utility connects garage and gym, and the east run is already organised for washing and folding.
items.proposal: Allocate a removable tray and small robust landing for muddy shoes, sports kit and shopping at the garage end.
items.benefit: Keeps dirty items off clean laundry and kitchen surfaces.
items.tradeoff: Must not consume the useful folding surface or narrow the door approach.
items.validation: Walk garage-to-utility with shopping and wet gym kit while an appliance is open.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Make laundry sorting and carrying easier
items.observation: The fitted run already includes two pull-out hamper bins and tall linen storage.
items.proposal: Refine bin heights, handles and a temporary basket perch so wet and clean loads can move through in sequence.
items.benefit: Improves use of the current layout without adding cabinets.
items.tradeoff: A basket perch can become clutter; it should fold away or be part of the counter.
items.validation: Demonstrate washer unloading, folding and carrying a full basket through both doorways.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Fit the garage to the actual household cars
items.observation: Current checks use two 4.40 x 1.80 m cars and 42-degree front-door openings; the arrangement is staggered.
items.proposal: Replace concept car envelopes with the household vehicles including mirrors, door travel and boot opening before fixing storage.
items.benefit: Protects the double-garage promise and avoids unusable fitted cupboards.
items.tradeoff: Larger cars may require less garage joinery or different staggering.
items.validation: Test driver/passenger exit and carrying shopping to the utility with both real cars parked.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Replan garage storage around a protected pedestrian strip
items.observation: Two staggered concept cars, storage, bicycles and the utility connection all compete for the garage floor.
items.proposal: Develop a complete garage layout with a clearly reserved pedestrian route to the utility, one consolidated perimeter storage wall and a genuinely retrievable bike zone. Keep two car spaces and the existing garage exterior/roof.
items.benefit: The garage becomes usable every day, with storage and walking routes designed around parked cars.
items.tradeoff: Some current cabinetry may have to move or shrink; larger real vehicles may rule out the desired bike arrangement.
items.validation: Use household vehicle envelopes, mirrors, boot and door travel, then show one person carrying shopping and one retrieving a bike.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Plan EV charging without trailing leads to the entrance
items.observation: The brief requires two garage spaces and four exterior parking spaces, creating several possible charging positions.
items.proposal: Develop discreet charger locations and cable reach to the likely daily vehicles, with capacity assessment before product choice.
items.benefit: Supports everyday charging while keeping pedestrian arrival clear.
items.tradeoff: Electrical supply and load management may govern the solution; not every bay needs a charger.
items.validation: Draw plugged-in vehicles and cables with the gate, boot and entrance routes in use.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Design the pool terrace as one complete outdoor room
items.observation: The pool, narrow edge routes, loungers and raised changing building work as separate elements; their transitions determine daily use.
items.proposal: Develop one coordinated pool-side layout with integrated cover housing, a clear wet route, usable lounging positions and a distinct dry seating edge. Preserve the pool, approved lounger orientation and external house form.
items.benefit: A coherent leisure space with better transitions and a deliberate relationship to changing and garden seating.
items.tradeoff: Cover mechanisms and accessible service space consume deck area; additional level changes must not be hidden by attractive paving.
items.validation: Render the pool covered/open and the walking route occupied, using the actual site levels and all deck clearances.
items.scope: Proposed only; existing-garden refinements separately assessed for Planning
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Make the pool-to-changing route comfortable when wet
items.observation: The summer house floor is raised above the pool terrace, and the existing route includes steps.
items.proposal: Detail a clearly lit wet route with consistent slip-resistant finishes and a well-resolved step/handhold arrangement; assess a gentle alternative only if it fits.
items.benefit: Improves the actual swimming routine while retaining the garden buildings.
items.tradeoff: A ramp could consume substantial garden space; do not claim level access without measured slopes.
items.validation: Draw levels and sections from pool edge to changing bench and WC, including nighttime use.
items.scope: Proposed only; existing-garden refinements separately assessed for Planning
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Turn the summer-house support rooms into a proper pool-changing suite
items.observation: The pool requires a convincing place to change, shower and handle wet towels, not only more storage furniture.
items.proposal: Study a dedicated shower/changing arrangement within the existing garden-building envelope, retaining the outside WC and relocating some tool storage to the workshop if necessary. Connect it to the existing changing bench and pool route.
items.benefit: Makes the pool function as a complete daily leisure facility without assuming a new garden building.
items.tradeoff: New drainage and ventilation are required; tool storage is displaced and the existing envelope may limit the shower size.
items.validation: Draw the full garden-building plan, privacy sequence, drying space and drainage route; retain useful workshop storage and realistic wet clearances.
items.scope: Proposed only; existing-garden refinements separately assessed for Planning
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Add a discreet rinse point near changing
items.observation: The pool and garden WC/changing area are separate connected spaces, with final services still unresolved.
items.proposal: Study a screened warm-water rinse point close to existing service routes, using the same stone/oak vocabulary.
items.benefit: Reduces water and dirt carried through the house and completes the pool routine.
items.tradeoff: Needs drainage, frost protection and privacy; omit if it cannot fit without crowding.
items.validation: Show screening sightlines, shower standing space and the dry pedestrian route.
items.scope: Proposed only; existing-garden refinements separately assessed for Planning
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Add a restrained covered poolside lounge
items.observation: The pool has sun loungers, but comfortable shade and dry outdoor sitting need a spatial solution beyond individual accessories.
items.proposal: Compare a modest freestanding pergola/covered lounge in the existing garden layout, using warm timber and pale upholstery, positioned to preserve the approved loungers and pool circulation. Keep its scale subordinate to the house.
items.benefit: Adds a distinct outdoor living destination and a useful connection between pool, garden and house.
items.tradeoff: It changes the exterior and introduces wind, drainage and potential planning implications; it is an option for review, not assumed permitted work.
items.validation: Show model views from house, pool and neighbouring boundaries; compare sun/shade and access before choosing location, footprint or roof type.
items.scope: Proposed only; existing-garden refinements separately assessed for Planning
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Keep pool equipment serviceable and acoustically discreet
items.observation: Pool/spa services are not resolved in the room study.
items.proposal: Reserve a properly ventilated equipment location with replacement access, pipe routes and noise separation from seating and neighbours.
items.benefit: Prevents plant from becoming an afterthought that spoils the garden.
items.tradeoff: A service enclosure consumes space and may need planning/design review.
items.validation: Show the largest equipment replacement path, drainage and an acoustic assessment before choosing enclosure details.
items.scope: Proposed only; existing-garden refinements separately assessed for Planning
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Give the garden a restrained evening lighting plan
items.observation: The scheme has pool, pavilion, workshop and several level changes rather than one simple lawn.
items.proposal: Develop a low-glare hierarchy for paths, steps and one or two planted focal points, with quiet late-night settings.
items.benefit: Makes the whole garden usable and coherent without floodlighting it.
items.tradeoff: Exterior light can disturb bedrooms, neighbours and wildlife; keep output and hours purposeful.
items.validation: Review views from seating, bedrooms and boundaries, with fittings aimed and shielded.
items.scope: Proposed only; existing-garden refinements separately assessed for Planning
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Refine the planting as year-round structure
items.observation: The model establishes mature trees and garden zones, but the owner-facing studies emphasise furniture more than seasonal planting.
items.proposal: Prepare a restrained planting concept with evergreen structure, softer seasonal layers and maintenance access around pool and paths.
items.benefit: Adds depth and individuality while supporting the accepted pool palette.
items.tradeoff: Plant size, roots, leaf fall and maintenance must suit the actual site; no tree removal is assumed.
items.validation: Show mature spread, winter appearance and clear paths, then coordinate with the arboricultural survey.
items.scope: Proposed only; existing-garden refinements separately assessed for Planning
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Compose the roof terrace as an outdoor living room
items.observation: The terrace contains three rooflights, guarding and privacy screens, which should lead the furniture arrangement.
items.proposal: Develop a complete terrace plan with a sheltered lounge, a compact serving point and an unobstructed door-to-outlook route around the rooflights. Integrate lightweight screening only where sightline checks justify it.
items.benefit: A purposeful outdoor room instead of furniture scattered around roof constraints.
items.tradeoff: Available seating area may shrink once realistic circulation, wind restraint, roof loading and drainage are accounted for.
items.validation: Render seated and standing views, rooflight access and occupied routes; coordinate the threshold, falls and structural limits separately.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Give terrace cushions and furniture a weather plan
items.observation: The design says loose cushions are stored indoors in bad weather; a cushion box already occupies part of the terrace.
items.proposal: Size storage to the actual cushion set and define secure furniture positions for wind without adding heavy planters casually.
items.benefit: Makes the terrace easier to use and close down.
items.tradeoff: Added weight and fixings affect structure/waterproofing; a box may not hold the whole set.
items.validation: Demonstrate all cushions stored and furniture restrained with rooflights and routes clear.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Balance terrace privacy with the seated outlook
items.observation: The terrace has a retained west privacy screen and two seating groups.
items.proposal: Check seated and standing neighbour sightlines, then refine only the necessary screen portions using the existing material family.
items.benefit: Avoids over-screening the terrace while protecting privacy where it matters.
items.tradeoff: Taller screens alter wind loading and the external appearance.
items.validation: Compare views from each seat and relevant neighbour windows against surveyed levels.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

references.title: Sevenoaks: Residential Extensions SPD (design and amenity guidance)

items.title: Design the workshop as a flexible creative studio
items.observation: The detached workshop has a main bench and mobile centre table, but its activities and storage need to define the layout.
items.proposal: Develop a complete workshop arrangement with a continuous tool/storage wall, a clear central assembly zone and a cleaner design/project corner. Separate dusty work from clean storage through layout and local extraction rather than filling every wall indiscriminately.
items.benefit: Turns the outbuilding into a useful second working destination with space for real projects.
items.tradeoff: The layout depends on the owner's tools and activities; extraction, power and noise provisions may be substantial.
items.validation: Show a large project on the centre table, tool access, material handling through the door and a cleared alternative state.
items.planCaption: Baseline plan only. This larger alternative requires its own coordinated model and occupied-use checks.

items.title: Make the workshop approach usable for carrying things
items.observation: The stepping stones have already been removed; the retained approach is a narrow garden strip route.
items.proposal: Refine a continuous firm surface, threshold and subtle lighting suitable for carrying a project or wheeled trolley.
items.benefit: Improves access without reintroducing the rejected stones.
items.tradeoff: Widening may affect planting and drainage; preserve the plot and tree constraints.
items.validation: Check actual path width, slope and doorway approach with the intended trolley or largest carried item.
items.planCaption: Existing brochure concept plan — shows the baseline, not this proposed improvement. Dimensions await survey.

items.title: Make brick setbacks read clearly in construction details
items.observation: The side-wing setback is 900 mm in the current specification, and front entrance/garage projections have repeatedly been flattened in images.
items.proposal: Develop coordinated corner, reveal and movement-joint details that preserve those real offsets in the model and drawing set.
items.benefit: Makes the brick composition legible and reduces ambiguous wall junctions.
items.tradeoff: Joint positions must follow construction design, not just visual preference.
items.validation: Compare plan, elevation and oblique native views with explicit offset dimensions.

references.title: Sevenoaks: Residential Extensions SPD (design and amenity guidance)

items.title: Resolve the garage-gable support with a real load path
items.observation: The accepted principal cross-wall and floor-concealed beam remain a structural concept, not engineered steelwork.
items.proposal: Ask the structural design to establish the floor-level beam, bearings and wall/opening support while retaining the garage roof form.
items.benefit: Addresses the owner's original support concern rather than merely improving the visible joint.
items.tradeoff: Beam depth or bearings may affect floors/partitions; any consequential design change needs separate review.
items.validation: Provide a section and load-path sketch tied to survey and structural calculations before claiming buildability.

items.title: Detail flat dormer caps and tiled cheeks consistently
items.observation: The owner requires tiled dormer fronts/cheeks but flat caps; generated images have repeatedly changed that roof shape.
items.proposal: Create one explicit dormer detail with cap edge, flashing, rainwater route and tile termination used by both designs and all visuals.
items.benefit: Preserves the intended architecture and makes the roof junction credible.
items.tradeoff: Real waterproofing edges may alter small visible dimensions.
items.validation: Check roof section and native close-up views before accepting any enhanced exterior image.

references.title: Sevenoaks: Residential Extensions SPD (design and amenity guidance)

items.title: Coordinate rainwater goods with the brick elevations
items.observation: The house combines original roofs, connector and front wing, creating several junctions and levels.
items.proposal: Review gutter/outlet/downpipe positions as a complete route and align them discreetly with existing corners where feasible.
items.benefit: Avoids arbitrary pipes interrupting glazing or ending above awkward roof junctions.
items.tradeoff: Drainage capacity and outlet placement can overrule visual symmetry.
items.validation: Trace every roof area to an outlet and lawful drainage strategy; show maintenance access.

items.title: Protect a clear pedestrian arrival through the forecourt
items.observation: The full brief retains four outside spaces alongside the double garage and gate.
items.proposal: Refine paving, lighting and parking positions to maintain an obvious route from gate and parked cars to the entrance.
items.benefit: Makes arrival safer and more welcoming without reducing the parking brief by stealth.
items.tradeoff: The fourth compact bay may constrain passage; actual vehicles and tracking decide feasibility.
items.validation: Test all six cars parked, gate open and one person carrying shopping to the front door.

references.title: Sevenoaks: Residential Extensions SPD (design and amenity guidance)

items.title: Design bins as a serviced part of the frontage
items.observation: The planning register says bin/cycle provision remains a concept requiring a workable layout.
items.proposal: Locate screened bin storage with ventilation, full lid opening and a practical collection-day route, using materials sympathetic to the brick frontage.
items.benefit: Avoids bins becoming the dominant entrance feature or blocking parking.
items.tradeoff: Storage can compete with gate visibility and planting; collection requirements need confirmation.
items.validation: Show bins in storage and being wheeled to collection with vehicles parked.

references.title: Sevenoaks: Residential Extensions SPD (design and amenity guidance)

items.title: Coordinate heating and ventilation with the furnished rooms
items.observation: Room studies repeatedly leave services unresolved, while furniture and glazing positions are now detailed.
items.proposal: Develop a whole-house service concept with plant space, ducts/pipe routes, accessible filters and room controls before more decorative detail.
items.benefit: Reduces late conflicts with wardrobes, ceilings and quiet rooms.
items.tradeoff: Services may require local boxing or reduced storage; assess options before choosing.
items.validation: Overlay routes with current furniture, structure and ceiling sections and identify every maintenance access point.

items.title: Give noisy rooms and bedrooms an acoustic adjacency plan
items.observation: The brief puts cinema/bar in the basement, gym in the front wing and sleeping rooms above/near leisure uses.
items.proposal: Map noise sources and quiet rooms, then develop targeted floor, partition and door strategies rather than treating every wall identically.
items.benefit: Protects sleep and study while retaining the full leisure brief.
items.tradeoff: Effective isolation may consume space or require construction changes.
items.validation: Review paths through floors, stairs, doors and services, not just surface finishes.

items.title: Plan summer comfort from the actual glazing and use
items.observation: Large garden glazing, a double-height entrance, loft rooms and multiple TVs create different comfort conditions.
items.proposal: Assess orientation, shading, secure ventilation and internal heat gains, prioritising passive measures before any cooling proposal.
items.benefit: Makes the home comfortable without adding visible equipment blindly.
items.tradeoff: A thermal assessment needs verified fabric/glazing and weather assumptions; applicability of regulations is separate.
items.validation: Compare overheating risk by room and show how selected measures affect the approved elevations.

references.title: Government: Approved Document O overview (check project applicability separately)

items.title: Keep future adaptability within the existing brief
items.observation: Most bedrooms have ensuites, while some routes and low-headroom areas are deliberately compact.
items.proposal: Identify a practical guest/sleeping and washing arrangement for temporary reduced mobility and reserve useful future service provisions.
items.benefit: Improves resilience without redesigning the whole house around an unrequested accessibility standard.
items.tradeoff: This may require a specific local doorway or fixture change; it is not a claim of full accessibility.
items.validation: Test the chosen everyday route and bathroom use with realistic assistance/space needs, then offer any building change separately.

items.title: Add a concise decision index to the long brochure
items.observation: The current brochure has 95 pages, 61 images and 27 area plans.
items.proposal: Add a clickable room index with page references and a short list of unresolved decisions, while keeping the full visual sequence.
items.benefit: Makes the expanded brochure useful for review rather than only browsing.
items.tradeoff: Another navigation layer must not duplicate several competing contents pages.
items.validation: Verify every link/page reference after pagination and test PDF navigation on desktop and tablet.

items.title: Show occupied-use plans beside the tightest rooms
items.observation: Several room plans look comfortable when furniture is unoccupied, while source reviews record single-file or shared-use constraints.
items.proposal: Add a small alternate diagram for cinema, games, gym, garage and compact bedrooms showing occupied chairs, doors and activity envelopes.
items.benefit: Makes the brochure honest about how spaces work without cluttering every architectural plan.
items.tradeoff: Diagrams need a clear legend and should not imply measured survey certainty.
items.validation: Cross-check each envelope against current specifications and label concept dimensions.

items.title: Use native geometry as the locked base for exterior photos
items.observation: Dormer caps and facade offsets have repeatedly drifted in enhanced exterior pictures.
items.proposal: Adopt a geometry-locked native render workflow for architecture, limiting enhancement to finishes, light and planting that preserve silhouettes/openings.
items.benefit: Improves credibility and reduces repeated corrections of beautiful but inaccurate images.
items.tradeoff: Native photorealism takes more lighting/material work and may be slower per image.
items.validation: Compare masks, edges, roof forms and openings against the native reference before publication.

items.title: Bring plans, sections and elevations onto one revision
items.observation: The principal gable change was patched into public models while native exports had a rebuild limitation; planning packs are separately generated.
items.proposal: Create one drawing issue with shared source hashes, room names, scale bars and sections through roof/level changes.
items.benefit: Makes the set more professional and exposes which documents reflect the latest design.
items.tradeoff: Full regeneration may require resolving the native build first; old issues should remain archived.
items.validation: Check source hashes and key dimensions across all drawings and state survey/concept status.

items.title: Add source-image comparisons to exterior review pages
items.observation: The site viewpoint markers already come from the camera manifest. The repeated problem has been visual differences between enhanced pictures and their native references.
items.proposal: Add a native/enhanced comparison control for exterior studies, with matched framing and a short record of approved appearance-only changes.
items.benefit: Lets the owner spot altered roofs, missing setbacks or invented openings immediately.
items.tradeoff: Two image sets add download weight; load the reference only when requested.
items.validation: Verify camera/framing correspondence and inspect dormer caps, facade offsets and openings at full resolution.

items.title: Make native and web model parity a release requirement
items.observation: A fresh read-only parse finds six principal-gable-wall parts in both public GLBs and none in their corresponding native geometry snapshots. Web and native-export-dependent outputs disagree on this feature.
items.proposal: Add a release report that compares design feature hashes and critical geometry across native, web, plans and brochure inputs.
items.benefit: Prevents one format silently lagging behind another after a targeted patch.
items.tradeoff: Requires reliable native export or an explicit blocked/stale status; do not mark parity from filenames alone.
items.validation: Deliberately stale one fixture export in a test and ensure the release report catches it.

items.title: Build only the changed room and dependent outputs
items.observation: The pipeline has room studies, source fingerprints and recent delivery caches; whole-design work is still costly for small changes.
items.proposal: Audit current dependency tracking and extend it so one room change invalidates only affected geometry, navigation, plans and images.
items.benefit: Makes iterative design faster while preserving correctness.
items.tradeoff: An incomplete dependency graph risks stale output; existing working caches should be reused.
items.validation: Compare a full clean build with incremental builds for room, roof and shared-material changes.

items.title: Add interior/exterior finish regression views
items.observation: Repeated owner corrections concerned exterior brick/white faces and interior reveals switching incorrectly.
items.proposal: Maintain fixed reference cameras and face classifications for both designs and all finish modes, including known troublesome walls.
items.benefit: Catches recurring finish mistakes before the owner sees them.
items.tradeoff: Image checks need tolerance for lighting; material/face assertions should support them.
items.validation: Exercise brick/render switches and verify internal faces, dormer cheeks and flat caps separately.

items.title: Load detailed room geometry when it is needed
items.observation: The models include tiny appliance and furniture details, while the deployed package remains large despite compression improvements.
items.proposal: Measure initial loading cost, then prototype room-based loading or distance detail levels that preserve close-up detail on demand.
items.benefit: Could make first entry and mobile browsing faster without deleting the details the owner requested.
items.tradeoff: Streaming boundaries can cause pop-in and navigation complexity; measure before committing.
items.validation: Compare cold-load time, memory, room-entry delay and visual parity on a representative phone and desktop.

items.title: Keep project status and approvals in one current register
items.observation: Several source JSON/Markdown files still say working, unapproved or unpublished after later integration and deployment.
items.proposal: Create a current issue register linking owner approvals, source revisions, verification and published release, with old notes marked historical.
items.benefit: Reduces confusion and prevents repeating completed work or treating outdated images as current.
items.tradeoff: Maintaining the register must be part of the normal build/review process, not another manual duplicate.
items.validation: Trace a room from approved brief through source, model, brochure and live release without contradictory current status.
